metadata.title: What Changed from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4? From Model Capability to Continuation Permission
metadata.description:
This paper reports a frozen, reproducible comparison of zero-visible-byte responses in gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 and gpt-4-0613. Both snapshots received identical semantic embodiment prompts through Chat Completions, with three null inputs, three matched controls, temperature 0, a 1,000-token completion ceiling, and ten fresh requests per input and model.

GPT-4 returned successful, present-string, zero-byte normal-stop responses on 30/30 null trials; GPT-3.5 returned visible text on all 30. Both models produced visible text on all 30 matched controls. All 120 requests returned HTTP 200, with zero retries, zero transport errors, and exact requested-to-returned model identifier matches. Raw-response reconstruction, frozen-source hashes, event-chain verification, and byte-identical analysis regeneration confirmed the recorded result.

The paper connects this served-system contrast to prior cross-vendor behavioral measurements and PCCG-2, a separate engineered causal demonstration in which continuation outcome changes while the complete non-EOS content-logit vector remains fixed. These distinct findings motivate studying continuation permission separately from content capability.

The comparison establishes a pinned-snapshot/model-family contrast, not a same-date historical emergence experiment. It does not identify the internal mechanism producing GPT-4’s empty responses, infer preserved latent answers from those responses, or equate provider stop metadata with direct observation of native EOS.

Exact prompts, request settings, raw provider responses, classifications, hashes, source code, and offline verification procedures are publicly available. The manuscript identifies the immutable result commit and reproduction commands.

title: What Changed from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4? From Model Capability to Continuation Permission
